newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends slightly up on wary buying.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends slightly up on wary buying.

text.p: Shenzhen B shares closed slightly higher on Friday in thin trading volume with investors awaiting for the flood of company annual reports due by April 30, brokers said.
The B share index inched up 0.07 points or 0.04 percent to 161.27 on turnover of HK$58.8 million, compared with Thursday's HK$44.1 million.
"Investors are cautious in the company report season, especially with talk that most companies are likely to offer unattractive dividend plans," an analyst with J&A Securities (Hong Kong) said.
Of the 44 B share companies listed in Shenzhen, only four have issued their 1996 results so far, with the April 30 deadline approaching.
Traders said they expected trading volume to remain thin and the index to flutter above the 160 point support next week.

"China's strong economic outlook is the major factor supporting the B index, but this spurs long-term investment rather than speculative moves," a broker said. China's State Statistical Bureau said China's economy would grow by 10 percent in 1997 with inflation around five percent, according to domestic media.
Brokers said gains on Friday's A share market may continue to push the B index up early next week.
The A index gained 5.65 points or 1.23 percent to 464.02 on turnover of 12.4 billion yuan against 7.4 billion yuan on Thursday.
"The B shares didn't move up as much as the A index because it takes time for foreign investors to react," an analyst with Sun Hung Kai Investment Services in Shenzhen said.
On the B share market, the biggest gainer was Shenzhen Great Ocean Shipping Co Ltd, up HK$0.11 or 2.95 percent to HK$3.84.
